comment: Took Religion, Sports, and Social Justice. Completely messed up my first essay but still managed to get an A-. Just be sure to participate in class and pay attention. Reading/watching assignments can be long but understand the concepts from the reading for good class discussion is all that matters.

This class is all readings, documentaries, and discussions. It can definently feel repetitive at times, but some topics are novel and interesting. Her grading is a but hard to understand. I struggled to get constructive and specific feedback on my written assignments. If you share her viewpoint, it tends to work in your favor.

This class is readings, documentaries, and discussions which often get repetitive and focus on the same themes. There were some interesting parts though. Her grading is a bit of a coin toss. I had a hard time getting feedback that was helpful. If you are taking this class for the gen eds, be ready to trudge through.

This class is readings, documentaries, and discussions, most of which are about black Muslim athletes. These can get repetitive quite quickly, but some are interesting. I struggled to understand some of her grading and did not receive much helpful feedback on my work.
Very nice teacher, class could have been very very boring if the class discussions weren't actually interesting. She wants to see you succeed in the class.

I had Dr. Hanaoka for the Life After Death topic and she was amazing. She's incredibly knowledgeable about what she teaches and genuinely cares to help you understand the topics. We did a lot of in class discussions on the readings which were helpful to understand the complicated topics.

Dr. Hanaoka is very knowledgeable about religion and sports, and she makes a class mostly about religion very interesting. Class discussions were always respectful and fun to take part in. Sometimes instructions for papers are a bit vague, but if you take the time to go to her office hours and talk with her about them, you will be fine.

Dr. Hanaoka is so kind and understanding there are no tests or quizzes in this class but there is some reading and she will cold call! But as long as you put in the work you will get your participation score she is super knowledgeable and will work with you if you're struggling
Dr. Hanaoka is amazing! She genuinely cares about her students. Surprisingly very generous about extensions and help outside of class. Highly recommend!
Amazing professor! Best class experience I've had at UR so far. Take a course with her if you can.

Dr. Hanaoka deserves her reputation as a tough professor, but she is an amazingly intelligent and you will get so much out of class with her if you put in the work. She is not as tough a grader as I expected, and she was very accessible to discuss assignments with. I gained so much from her class!
Please do not take this professor
Hardest FYS at this school. Her essay prompts were long-winded and unclear, even her own writing consultants could not understand them.

Extremely hard professor. Super nice and knowledgeable but not understanding whatsoever. Ridiculous amount of reading and grades papers super harshly, and ALL of her feedback is non specific and just automated copied messages that she uses on all papers. Do not take this professor, your gpa will drop and you will regret it.

Prof. Hanaoka means well but would not take for an FYS again. Her workload is not terrible but she was definitely a tough grader and her prompts were often confusing and broad. Her class was all discussion oriented and not horrible but for someone who is not interested in the subject I would not recommend.

I didn't expect much entering this course but Professor Hanaoka made it pretty interesting. She is passionate about the subject and pretty accessible out of class if you ever need to discuss an idea. However, you'll get three papers and a presentation for the semester. Prepare to write.
This is a great choice for FYS. Mimi Hanaoka is an amazing professor who really knows her stuff and makes it super interesting for first year students. I will definitely take a course with her again.

Dr. Hanaoka is extremely intelligent and knowledgeable, and I learned a lot from her class. However, her grading criteria and prompts are extremely long that it makes it confusing to figure out what she is asking for. She expects students to write papers a specific way that is quite different from other essay formats or structures, grading harshly.
Dr. Hanaoka is an amazing professor that cares about her students a lot. I'll definitely recommend her to others.
One of the best professors I've had at UR
This was my only course in religious studies and it was amazing. Hanaoka is one of my favorite professors at UR.
Tough but excellent professor. Really interesting readings.
Dr. Hanaoka is everything I hoped and feared a college professor would be. She makes you work hard and you learn more than you thought was possible. If you actually do the work, you'll get an A.
My favorite professor at UR. She's truly inspirational and I can't wait to take another class with her.
Excellent

Do not take this FYS. It is way too much work to be an FYS and she is a very tough grader. Class content is difficult to understand. Feedback on the essays is pretty useless, as she often writes vague and doesn't give specifics.

Hardest FYS class ever. Taking her is def my biggest regret. She kills you gpa- no kidding. People in the class are getting Cs and Ds - and we spent at least 3 hours to do the reading for EVERY class. She grades extremely harshly on papers - it's hard to get above a C. She killed my soul.

Unless you want to abandon all other responsibilities, you won't get an A. This class is very demanding for an incoming freshman. While the content is interesting, there is just so much. If you do have Dr. Hanaoka, do not slack off on the readings.

my biggest regret is taking her FYS class. Not only was all the info useless, but she also grades very severely and vaguely. For my first paper she said that my footnotes were correct but on my next paper she took away a lot of points cause "i did the footnotes completely wrong" even though i literally did the same thing

probably the hardest FYS class. She grades so harshly that it makes me mad since an FYS is all about teaching freshman how to write good research papers and all she does is give you a vague essay prompt and expects you to write a professional research paper without teaching you anything.

Hanaoka is the most vigorous professor I have ever had. Ensures students that they must spend 14 hours a week in preparation for this class in order to do well. Unless you are extremely interested in Islam I would take the class. When a paper is due she also assigns a couple hours of reading as well.

Such an amazing and inspiring professor. She is very intelligent and passionate about her teaching. Amazing discussions and interesting material. She's a tough grader and does not give much help for papers which makes it difficult to get a good grade.

Professor Hanaoka is a great teacher.  She is really passionate about Islamic studies and is really good at getting her students to engage in the material.  However, she's a pretty tough grader and expects a lot out of her students.  If you do the work, you'll be fine.

Professor Hanaoka is a tough teacher. But she's very intelligent and her class was always interesting (you really do learn a lot). She tells you to not worry about grades and I honestly think you shouldn't (she gives you extra credit opportunities and essay re-visions). So just enjoy learning, work hard, and I promise you'll get the A.

Professor Hanaoka I felt was engaging and highly interested in her subject. The readings are long and sometimes tedious, but the subject is great. Very knowledgeable and clear. Pay attention in class and you will be fine.  Primary assignments are essays, uses Chicago style for citing sources. Make sure you know what that is.
